items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — B.Tech Course Categories
The B.Tech curriculum contains the following categories of courses.
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: B.Tech Course Categories

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — AEC — Ability Enhancement Courses
Ability Enhancement Courses are based on content intended to enhance knowledge through various areas of study.

They include:

- Language and Literature
- Indian Knowledge System
- Environmental Science and Sustainable Development

These are mandatory for all disciplines, and some may be chosen from a pool of courses.

**Indicative share: 3%-4%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: AEC — Ability Enhancement Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — VAC — Value Added Courses
Value Added Courses are intended to inculcate:

- Ethics
- Culture
- Constitutional values
- Soft skills
- Sports education
- Similar areas supporting all-round development

Some courses may be chosen from a pool.

**Indicative share: 3%-4%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: VAC — Value Added Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — SEC — Skill Enhancement Courses
Skill Enhancement Courses are skill-based courses intended to provide:

- Hands-on training
- Competencies
- Practical skills

**Indicative share: 2%-3%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: SEC — Skill Enhancement Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — IEC — Interdisciplinary Engineering Courses
These are basic interdisciplinary engineering courses from areas such as:

- Information Technology
- Electronics
- Automation

The courses are from areas other than the student's programme of study.

**Indicative share: 14%-20%**

For Mathematics and Computing (MNC):

**Indicative share: 25%-30%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: IEC — Interdisciplinary Engineering Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — PCC — Program Core Courses
Program Core Courses are mandatory courses considered essential for the chosen engineering/science discipline.

**Indicative share: 27%-35%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: PCC — Program Core Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — PEC — Program Elective Courses
Each branch offers a variety of elective courses.

These courses provide students with opportunities to:

- Discover academic interests
- Choose courses from their programme's elective pool
- Enhance engagement in the learning process

Such courses are termed Program Elective Courses (PEC).

**Indicative share: 9%-14%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: PEC — Program Elective Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — OEC — Open Elective Courses
Open Elective Courses provide multidisciplinary or interdisciplinary education.

When a student chooses a PEC/PCC offered by another department, that course is treated as an Open Elective Course (OEC) for that student.

**Indicative share: 9%-14%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: OEC — Open Elective Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — MMC — Mandatory Mathematics Courses
Mandatory Mathematics Courses are required for each discipline except Mathematics and Computing.

**Indicative share: 7%-10%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: MMC — Mandatory Mathematics Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Course Categories — PIR — Project, Internship and Research
PIR includes:

- Engineering projects
- Research projects
- Internships
- Summer internships
- Summer projects

**Indicative share: 9%-14%**
items.title: B.Tech Course Categories
items.heading: PIR — Project, Internship and Research

items.text:
Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning — Flexible Course Timing
The semester mentioned for the following courses is indicative and suggested:

- Program Elective Courses (PECs)
- Open Elective Courses (OECs)
- Non-Mandatory AECs
- Non-Mandatory VACs

These courses may be completed earlier or later than the suggested semester.
items.title: Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning
items.heading: Flexible Course Timing

items.text:
Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning — Prerequisites
If a student wishes to take a course earlier than its scheduled semester, the student must consider the prerequisite requirements.

The student must ensure that the prerequisite requirements of the course are satisfied.
items.title: Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning
items.heading: Prerequisites

items.text:
Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning — Course Availability
The student must also ensure that the desired course is offered in a free slot in the semester in which the student wants to take it.
items.title: Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning
items.heading: Course Availability

items.text:
Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning — Maximum Semester Credit Load
The maximum number of credits a student may take in one semester, including backlog credits, is:

**32 credits**
items.title: Course Load and Fast and Slow Learning
items.heading: Maximum Semester Credit Load

items.text:
B.Tech Course Structure and L-T-P-C Format — 11.1 Course Structure
A student shall register for theory and practical courses each semester according to the respective Course Structure prescribed by the Senate.

Each course carries a weight in terms of credit units depending on the nature of the course, such as theory or practical.

The credit is determined by the expected contact hours, including:

- Lecture hours
- Tutorial hours
- Laboratory hours
- Additional hours that a student is expected to devote per week
items.title: B.Tech Course Structure and L-T-P-C Format
items.heading: 11.1 Course Structure

items.text:
B.Tech Course Structure and L-T-P-C Format — L-T-P-C Format
Every course is associated with a four-tuple:

**L-T-P-C**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| L | Number of Lecture Hours per week |
| T | Number of Tutorial Hours per week |
| P | Number of Practical/Laboratory Hours per week |
| C | Credit of the course |
items.title: B.Tech Course Structure and L-T-P-C Format
items.heading: L-T-P-C Format

items.text:
B.Tech Course Structure and L-T-P-C Format — 11.2 General Credit Pattern
Except for Internship/Projects, credits are assigned according to the following general pattern:

| Activity | Credits |
|---|---:|
| Each Lecture period per week | 1 credit |
| Each Tutorial period per week | 1 credit |
| Three-hour Practical/Laboratory Session per week | 3 credits |
| Two-hour Practical/Laboratory Session per week | 2 credits |
items.title: B.Tech Course Structure and L-T-P-C Format
items.heading: 11.2 General Credit Pattern

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — 12.1 Credit Requirement
To qualify for a B.Tech degree, a student must complete the credit requirement prescribed in the Course Structure for the particular programme.

The credit requirement for a programme is:

**164–172 credits**
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: 12.1 Credit Requirement

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — Equivalent Courses
If a student has to take courses different from those prescribed in the Course Structure because of backlog cases, semester-drop cases or similar circumstances, the student must complete the exact number of equivalent courses decided by the DUPC.
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: Equivalent Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — NPTEL/SWAYAM for Theoretical Backlogs
If a student has a backlog in a theoretical course with no laboratory component, the student may opt for a course offered by NPTEL/SWAYAM having equivalent course credit.

The student's progress will be monitored by a nominated faculty member of the concerned department.

Permission in such cases is granted by the IUPC on the recommendation of the DUPC.
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: NPTEL/SWAYAM for Theoretical Backlogs

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — 12.2 Extra Courses and Backlogs
Students may be permitted to take extra courses on the recommendation of the Faculty Advisor and approval of the Department Undergraduate Programme Committee (DUPC).
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: 12.2 Extra Courses and Backlogs

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — 12.2.1 Backlog Courses
Students who have failed with an "F" grade in one or more subjects in previous Autumn/Spring semesters may register in the next semester for:

**At most two theory backlog courses**

This is allowed only if the courses are offered in that semester.

A student with due backlog courses may register for Summer School for:

**At most 10 credits**

subject to the applicable provisions and course availability.
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: 12.2.1 Backlog Courses

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — 12.2.2 Semester Drop
A student who has dropped a semester because of critical disease, accident or calamity will be allowed to register for the subsequent semester.

Such a student may be allowed to register for extra courses, including backlog courses, subject to the limits specified in the ordinance:

- Maximum two theory courses; or
- Two theory courses with laboratory components.

This applies when the corresponding courses are offered.
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: 12.2.2 Semester Drop

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — 12.2.3 Dropping PEC/OEC
Students are allowed to drop only:

- One Program Elective Course (PEC); or
- One Open Elective Course (OEC)

per semester.

An equivalent or alternate course may be permitted in a later semester.
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: 12.2.3 Dropping PEC/OEC

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — 12.3 Curriculum and Syllabi
Every undergraduate programme has a curriculum and syllabi for courses approved by the Senate.

The DUPC discusses and recommends undergraduate course syllabi before sending them to the Institute Undergraduate Programme Committee (IUPC).

The IUPC considers departmental proposals and recommends them to the Senate for consideration and approval.
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: 12.3 Curriculum and Syllabi

items.text:
B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules — 12.4 Medium of Instruction
The medium of:

- Instruction
- Examination
- Project reports

shall be **English**.
items.title: B.Tech Credit Requirement and Backlog Rules
items.heading: 12.4 Medium of Instruction

items.text:
Grading System — 17.1 Awarding of Grades
At the end of a semester or Summer School, the concerned Course Instructor awards a letter grade for each course.

The instructor considers the student's performance in:

- Quizzes
- Assignments
- Mid-semester examination
- End-semester examination
- Viva
- Laboratory work
- Attendance and regularity in classes

Grades are submitted by the Course Instructor through a signed grade sheet in the prescribed format.

The grade sheet is submitted to the office of the Head of Department within the prescribed time after the End-Semester or Supplementary Examination.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: 17.1 Awarding of Grades

items.text:
Grading System — Letter Grades and Grade Points
The Institute uses the following letter grades:

| Letter Grade | Academic Performance | Grade Point |
|---|---|---:|
| O | Outstanding | 10 |
| A | Excellent | 9 |
| B | Very Good | 8 |
| C | Good | 7 |
| D | Average | 6 |
| P | Below Average | 5 |
| F | Fail | 0 |
| I | Incomplete | — |
| X | Debarred | — |

The grades **I** and **X** are transitional grades representing:

- **I:** Incomplete
- **X:** Debarred
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: Letter Grades and Grade Points

items.text:
Grading System — 17.2 Relative Grading System
When a course is taught by more than one teacher for different batches, a committee consisting of:

- Course Coordinator — Chairperson
- Other faculty members teaching the course — Members

will finalize the grades.

If necessary, marks from different batches may be normalized before final grades are awarded.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: 17.2 Relative Grading System

items.text:
Grading System — Minimum Requirement for Passing
No student who has obtained **35% or more marks** should be awarded the failing grade **F**.

The Chairman, Senate may constitute a committee chaired by the Dean/Associate Dean of Academic Affairs to examine grades awarded in a course if required.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: Minimum Requirement for Passing

items.text:
Grading System — Normal Distribution Guideline
The ordinance provides a relative grading guideline based on:

- Mean marks: X̄
- Standard deviation: s

The guideline provides approximate distributions for grades O, A, B, C, D, P and F.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: Normal Distribution Guideline

items.text:
Grading System — 17.3 Absence from End-Semester Examination
A student who does not appear in the End-Semester Examination for any reason is awarded an:

**F grade**

This applies irrespective of performance in the Mid-Semester Examination and Sessional Awards.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: 17.3 Absence from End-Semester Examination

items.id: academics/grading-system.md::17.4 Successful Completion of a Course::0
items.text:
Grading System — 17.4 Successful Completion of a Course
A student successfully completes a subject and earns its credits when the student receives a letter grade other than:

- I
- X
- F

An **F grade** in any subject means failure in that subject.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: 17.4 Successful Completion of a Course

items.text:
Grading System — Grade I — Incomplete
A teacher may award an **I grade** when a student was compelled to miss the End-Semester Examination because of:

- Illness
- Accident that prevented the student from appearing in the examination
- Natural disaster or calamity during the End-Semester Examination that, in the opinion of the Institute, required the student to leave the campus

The student is eligible for an I grade only when:

- Attendance is complete and satisfactory.
- Performance in other assessment components is complete and satisfactory.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: Grade I — Incomplete

items.text:
Grading System — Grade X — Debarred
A student may receive an **X grade** after being debarred from an End-Semester Examination due to:

1. Unsatisfactory attendance.
2. Disciplinary action by the Institute.
3. Recommendation of the Unfair Means Committee for malpractice in an examination.

If debarred because of attendance, attendance below **50%** results in debarment from the End-Semester Examination in that course.

A student awarded an X grade may re-register for the relevant subject or semester after the debarment period expires, provided that other provisions of the regulations do not prevent the student from doing so.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: Grade X — Debarred

items.text:
Grading System — Conversion of I Grade
An I grade is converted to a letter grade after successful clearance in a Supplementary Examination conducted in July each year.
items.title: Grading System
items.heading: Conversion of I Grade

items.text:
B.Tech Honours Degree — 14.1 Requirements
A student who wishes to pursue the B.Tech (Honours) degree must:

- Earn **8 additional credits**.
- Have a **CGPA of 8.0 or more**, excluding Additional Credits.
- Complete the prescribed undergraduate research work.
items.title: B.Tech Honours Degree
items.heading: 14.1 Requirements

items.text:
B.Tech Honours Degree — Research Requirement
At least **4 of the 8 additional credits** must be earned through Undergraduate Research Work.

The research work must result in the publication of at least **one research paper** in an SCI/SCIE/SCOPUS journal in a relevant area.

The assigned guide/supervisor(s) from the Institute will be co-author(s).

The total number of students who are co-authors of the paper cannot be more than **two**.

There cannot be any other co-author from inside or outside the Institute.
items.title: B.Tech Honours Degree
items.heading: Research Requirement

items.text:
B.Tech Honours Degree — Remaining 4 Credits
The remaining **4 additional credits** may be completed through Program Elective Courses (PEC).

These courses may be completed through:

- SWAYAM
- NPTEL

The additional course must not be equivalent to:

- A course already taken by the student; or
- A course that the student will later take as a requirement for completing the B.Tech degree.
items.title: B.Tech Honours Degree
items.heading: Remaining 4 Credits

items.text:
B.Tech Honours Degree — 14.3 CGPA Calculation
The additional **8 credits** earned for the Honours degree are **not considered** while calculating CGPA.
items.title: B.Tech Honours Degree
items.heading: 14.3 CGPA Calculation

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.1 Minor Discipline
Students may opt for a Minor in a discipline other than the discipline in which they were originally admitted.

The Minor will be mentioned in:

- The degree certificate
- The final grade card

The original branch remains the student's Major.

For example:

**Major:** Electronics and Communication Engineering  
**Minor:** Computer Science and Engineering
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.1 Minor Discipline

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.2 Requirements for Minor
A four-year B.Tech degree with a Minor in a specific domain requires:

- Completion of the four-year degree programme.
- Completion of **172 credits**.
- Satisfaction of the prescribed credit requirements.
- Earning **8 additional credits** through 2 Open Elective Courses (OECs).
- Earning a minimum of **5 OECs**, including the 2 additional OECs, from the basket of courses prescribed for the particular Minor.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.2 Requirements for Minor

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.3 Minor Course Structure
For every Minor discipline, the courses are finalized by the Senate.

The courses are proposed by the IUPC based on the recommendation of the DUPC of the concerned department.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.3 Minor Course Structure

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.4 Eligibility to Apply
Only students who have completed all credits required in their first two semesters are eligible to apply for a Minor discipline.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.4 Eligibility to Apply

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.5 Application
Students must apply for a Minor using the prescribed form.

The Academic Section calls for applications at the end of the second semester of each academic year.

Completed applications must be submitted by the last date specified in the notification.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.5 Application

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.6 Intake
The intake for every Minor discipline is decided by the Academic Section in consultation with the respective Head of Department.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.6 Intake

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.7 Choice of Minor
Students may list their preferred Minor disciplines in order of preference.

Once the application has been submitted, the choices cannot be changed.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.7 Choice of Minor

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.8 Selection
Selection to Minor disciplines is based strictly on merit according to the CGPA of applicants, depending on:

- Available intake
- Number of applications received
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.8 Selection

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.9 Starting the Minor
The Minor becomes effective from the student's **third semester**.

No change of Minor discipline is permitted after this.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.9 Starting the Minor

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.10 Dropping an Open Elective
A student will not be eligible for the Minor degree if the student drops an Open Elective and subsequently takes another Open Elective from a different basket.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.10 Dropping an Open Elective

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.11 Minor Backlog
A backlog course in the Minor discipline may be cleared during the summer term through a supplementary examination.

Failing again in the supplementary examination will result in dropping of the Minor discipline.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.11 Minor Backlog

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.12 SGPA and CGPA Calculation
For a student pursuing a Minor, after completing at least two semesters:

- Five OECs are associated with the Minor basket.
- The best **3 out of 5 OECs** are considered for CGPA calculation.
- The remaining 2 OECs are not counted in CGPA.
- The CGPA calculation is therefore based on **164 credits** after completing 172 credits.

If necessary, the SGPA of a particular semester may be upgraded when an OEC from that semester is not counted in the CGPA.

The final mark sheet will contain a separate section listing:

- All Minor courses
- The 3 OECs counted in CGPA
- The 2 OECs not counted in CGPA
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.12 SGPA and CGPA Calculation

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.13 Dropping the Minor
If the Minor discipline is dropped, successfully completed extra courses may be mentioned in a separate certificate upon the student's request.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.13 Dropping the Minor

items.text:
Major and Minor Degree — 13.14 Opting Out
A student may opt out of the Minor discipline by submitting the prescribed form.

Once a student opts out, the student cannot rejoin the Minor discipline.
items.title: Major and Minor Degree
items.heading: 13.14 Opting Out

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
Section 12.5 provides multiple exit options from the undergraduate programme.
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — Exit-1: After First Year
A student who exits after completing the first year and has secured a minimum of:

**40 credits**

may receive a **UG Certificate** if the student also earns:

**4 credits**

through one of the following during the first-year summer vacation:

- Two-month summer internship
- ITI-level courses
- Skill-based courses
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: Exit-1: After First Year

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — Exit-2: After Second Year
A student who exits after completing the second year and has secured a minimum of:

**80 credits**

may receive a **UG Diploma** if the student also earns:

**4 credits**

through one of the following during the second-year summer vacation:

- Two-month summer internship
- Diploma-level courses
- Skill-based courses
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: Exit-2: After Second Year

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — Exit-3: After Third Year
A student who exits after completing the third year and has secured a minimum of:

**120 credits**

may receive a:

**B.Voc Degree in the Major discipline**

The student must additionally complete a:

**4-credit summer internship**

during the third-year summer vacation.
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: Exit-3: After Third Year

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — B.Tech
The four-year B.Tech degree in the Major discipline is awarded to students who:

- Complete the four-year degree programme.
- Complete 164 credits.
- Satisfy the credit requirements.
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: B.Tech

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — B.Tech (Honours)
The four-year B.Tech (Honours) degree in the Major discipline is awarded to students who:

- Complete the four-year degree programme.
- Complete 172 credits.
- Have a CGPA of 8.0 or more, excluding Additional Credits.

Detailed Honours regulations are given in Section 14.
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: B.Tech (Honours)

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — B.Tech with Major and Minor
The four-year B.Tech degree with a minor in a specific domain is awarded to students who:

- Complete the four-year degree programme.
- Complete 172 credits.
- Satisfy the applicable credit requirements.

Detailed Minor regulations are given in Section 13.
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: B.Tech with Major and Minor

items.text:
Multiple Exit and Re-Entry — Re-Entry
Students using the multiple-exit provisions are allowed to re-enter the degree programme within:

**3 years**

They must complete the degree programme within the stipulated maximum period of:

**7 years**
items.title: Multiple Exit and Re-Entry
items.heading: Re-Entry

items.text:
Online and External Course Credits — Online and External Course Credits
Course credits may be earned in online/offline mode from online portals or other institutes/universities.

Prior approval of the Department Undergraduate Program Committee (DUPC) of the respective department is required.

The ordinance specifies the following category-wise maximum limits:

| Course Category | Maximum Credits | Permitted Sources |
|---|---:|---|
| VAC/AEC | 11 credits | SWAYAM, NPTEL, Coursera, Udemy, EdX |
| PEC/OEC | 20 credits | SWAYAM, NPTEL |
items.title: Online and External Course Credits
items.heading: Online and External Course Credits

items.text:
Online and External Course Credits — Approval Requirement
The student must obtain prior approval from the concerned Department Undergraduate Program Committee (DUPC).
items.title: Online and External Course Credits
items.heading: Approval Requirement

items.text:
B.Tech Admission Rules — B.Tech Admission
The number of seats in each undergraduate branch is decided by the Senate and approved by the Governing Body/Board of Governors of IIIT Bhagalpur.

Reservation is governed by applicable Ministry of Education/Government of India guidelines.

Admission to the B.Tech programme is made in the Autumn Semester at the first-year level through JEE-Main, conducted by the National Testing Agency under the supervision of the Joint Admission Board. The Institute follows applicable Ministry of Education guidelines for undergraduate admission.

If, after admission, it is found that a candidate did not fulfil the requirements stated in the admission offer, the Senate Chairperson may revoke the admission on the recommendation of the Dean/Associate Dean of Academic Affairs and report the matter to the Senate.

The Institute may also cancel a student's admission and require discontinuation of studies because of unsatisfactory academic performance or disciplinary grounds. Academic-performance criteria are governed by the B.Tech rules and regulations, while disciplinary matters are governed by the applicable student code and conduct rules.
items.title: B.Tech Admission Rules
items.heading: B.Tech Admission

items.text:
Student Exchange and Credit Transfer — Student Exchange and Credit Transfer
A B.Tech student who is permitted to attend another institute or university in India or abroad under an exchange programme or other approved arrangement may have credits earned at that institution transferred as earned credits.

If the course or research work completed at the other institution has not been evaluated there, IIIT Bhagalpur may evaluate it for equivalent credit. The resulting earned credit is then credited to the student's academic record.

The exact credit-transfer treatment is therefore subject to the Institute's applicable approval and evaluation process.
items.title: Student Exchange and Credit Transfer
items.heading: Student Exchange and Credit Transfer

items.text:
Attendance Requirements — 8.1 General Attendance
Students are required to attend all classes for which they have registered.

This includes:

- Lectures
- Tutorials
- Laboratories
- Practical sessions
- Workshops
items.title: Attendance Requirements
items.heading: 8.1 General Attendance

items.text:
Attendance Requirements — 8.2 Minimum Attendance
Students must maintain a minimum attendance of **75%**, taking medical, calamity and disaster-related absence into consideration.

The following consequences apply:

| Attendance | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Below 50% | The student is debarred from appearing in the End-Semester Examination and is awarded an "F" grade in the course. |
| 50% to below 75% | One grade is reduced from the student's secured grade in the concerned course, except when the secured grade is "P". |
| 75% or above | The minimum attendance requirement is satisfied, subject to the other provisions of the ordinance. |
items.title: Attendance Requirements
items.heading: 8.2 Minimum Attendance

items.id: attendance/attendance.md::8.3 Temporary Absence for Approved Activities::0
items.text:
Attendance Requirements — 8.3 Temporary Absence for Approved Activities
A student's temporary absence for activities such as:

- Technical festivals
- Technical competitions
- Cultural meets
- Sports meets
- Academic workshops
- Academic conferences
- Research visits

may be condoned for attendance.

Such absence is subject to recommendation by the Faculty in-charge of Student Affairs or Faculty in-charge of Academic Affairs and the Head of the concerned department, followed by approval by the Director.
items.title: Attendance Requirements
items.heading: 8.3 Temporary Absence for Approved Activities

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — 15.1 Regular Examinations
The Institute follows a system of continuous assessment for evaluating students.

For theoretical courses, assessment includes:

- Quizzes
- Assignments
- Tutorials
- Internal assessment
- Attendance
- Mid-semester examination
- End-semester examination
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: 15.1 Regular Examinations

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — Laboratory Courses
For laboratory courses, continuous assessment includes:

- Attendance
- Laboratory report submission
- Performance evaluation after each laboratory session
- End-semester examination
- Viva
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: Laboratory Courses

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — Project Evaluation
Project evaluation includes:

- Submission of the project report
- Seminar
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: Project Evaluation

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — Eligibility
Students who have been awarded any of the following grades are eligible for a supplementary examination:

- F
- I
- X
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: Eligibility

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — Timing
The supplementary examination is conducted during **May–July (summer term)** every year.

Students must register for supplementary courses by:

- Paying the prescribed fees.
- Registering within the stipulated time in the Academic Calendar.
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: Timing

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — Late Registration
For late registration, students must obtain approval from the Dean/Associate Dean (Academics) within **7 days** from the date of registration in the summer term specified in the Academic Calendar.

The late fee remains the same as that applicable to the Spring/Autumn semester.
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: Late Registration

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — Supplementary Examination Weightage
For a supplementary examination:

- Internal assessment carries **20% weightage** and is carried over from the concerned semester.
- Marks obtained in the supplementary examination carry **80% weightage**.

These components are considered for preparation of the new grade.
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: Supplementary Examination Weightage

items.text:
Examination and Supplementary Examination — Maximum Credits
A student may appear for supplementary examinations for a maximum of:

**15 credits**

in one summer term.
items.title: Examination and Supplementary Examination
items.heading: Maximum Credits

items.text:
Summer School — 16.1 Eligibility
Students who are eligible to appear for a supplementary examination in a particular course are also eligible to register for that course in the Summer School.

The Summer School normally runs from:

**Last week of May or first week of June to the last week of July.**
items.title: Summer School
items.heading: 16.1 Eligibility

items.text:
Summer School — Minimum Number of Students
A Summer School for a particular course can be conducted only when:

- At least **5 eligible candidates** have applied for that course.
- Suitable and available faculty members are found to conduct the course.
items.title: Summer School
items.heading: Minimum Number of Students

items.text:
Summer School — Assessment
Assessment of a Summer School course is similar to the assessment followed in:

- Autumn Semester
- Spring Semester

The concerned department retains the semester performance records of the students.
items.title: Summer School
items.heading: Assessment

items.id: examinations/summer-school.md::16.2 Offering a Summer School Course::0
items.text:
Summer School — 16.2 Offering a Summer School Course
A department may offer a Summer School course:

1. On the recommendation of the DUPC.
2. With approval of the Dean/Associate Dean of Academic Affairs.

A student may register for a maximum of:

**12 credits**

during a summer term.
items.title: Summer School
items.heading: 16.2 Offering a Summer School Course

items.text:
Summer School — 16.3 Announcement and Registration
Summer School courses are announced by the Academic Affairs Office at the end of the even semester before the commencement of the End-Semester Examination.

Students must register for Summer School courses by:

- Paying the prescribed fees.
- Registering within the stipulated time specified in the announcement.
items.title: Summer School
items.heading: 16.3 Announcement and Registration

items.text:
Summer School — 16.4 Semester Drop Students
Students who have been granted a semester drop by the Chairman, Senate, on grounds such as:

- Medical reasons
- Calamity
- Natural disaster

may be allowed to clear the concerned courses during the Summer Term.

The applicable conditions are those specified under Clause 12.2.2.
items.title: Summer School
items.heading: 16.4 Semester Drop Students

items.text:
Leave of Absence — Short Duration Leave
If the period of leave is less than two weeks, the student must submit a prior application for leave to the Head of the concerned department.

The application must:

- Mention valid reasons for the leave.
- Include supporting documents.

The leave is granted by the Head of the department.
items.title: Leave of Absence
items.heading: Short Duration Leave

items.id: leave/leave-of-absence.md::Leave Likely to Exceed Two Weeks::0
items.text:
Leave of Absence — Leave Likely to Exceed Two Weeks
If the period of absence is likely to exceed two weeks, a prior application for leave must be submitted through the Head of the Department to the Dean/Associate Dean of Academic Affairs.

Supporting documents must be provided.
items.title: Leave of Absence
items.heading: Leave Likely to Exceed Two Weeks

items.text:
Leave of Absence — Absence Exceeding Four Weeks
If a student remains absent for more than four weeks, the Dean/Associate Dean of Academic Affairs may ask the student to drop the semester.
items.title: Leave of Absence
items.heading: Absence Exceeding Four Weeks

items.text:
Leave of Absence — Effect on Attendance
Leave of absence under Clauses 9.1(a) and 9.1(b) will **not be condoned for attendance**.
items.title: Leave of Absence
items.heading: Effect on Attendance

items.text:
Leave of Absence — 9.2 Responsibility to Inform Authorities
Before availing leave, the student is responsible for informing:

- The Warden of the hostel in which the student resides.
- The concerned instructors.
items.title: Leave of Absence
items.heading: 9.2 Responsibility to Inform Authorities

items.text:
Leave of Absence — 9.3 Relaxation in Exceptional Circumstances
In exceptional circumstances, the Director may relax any of the above requirements on the recommendation of the Dean/Associate Dean of Academic Affairs.
items.title: Leave of Absence
items.heading: 9.3 Relaxation in Exceptional Circumstances

items.text:
Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme — 9.4 Eligibility for Temporary Withdrawal
A student admitted to an undergraduate programme may be permitted to withdraw temporarily for one semester or more on grounds such as:

- Prolonged illness
- Grave calamity in the family

The temporary withdrawal is subject to the conditions specified below.
items.title: Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme
items.heading: 9.4 Eligibility for Temporary Withdrawal

items.text:
Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme — Application
The student must apply to the Institute within at least **four weeks** of:

- The commencement of the semester; or
- The date the student last attended classes,

whichever is later.

The application must:

- State the reasons for withdrawal.
- Include supporting documents.
- Include endorsement of the student's guardian.
items.title: Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme
items.heading: Application

items.text:
Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme — Completion Requirement
The Institute must be satisfied that, even after counting the period of withdrawal, the student is likely to complete the B.Tech degree requirements within the specified time limits.
items.title: Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme
items.heading: Completion Requirement

items.text:
Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme — Outstanding Dues
The student must have no outstanding dues or demands with:

- Institute
- Hostel
- Department
- Library
- NSS
- NCC
items.title: Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme
items.heading: Outstanding Dues

items.text:
Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme — 9.5 Maximum Withdrawal
Normally, a student will be permitted only **one such temporary withdrawal** during the undergraduate programme.

The total temporary withdrawal period must not exceed **one year**.
items.title: Temporary Withdrawal from Undergraduate Programme
items.heading: 9.5 Maximum Withdrawal

items.title: Academic Affairs Administration
items.heading: Academic Affairs Administration

items.text:
Academic Calendar — Academic Calendar
The Institute academic session is divided into two regular semesters:

- Autumn Semester
- Spring Semester

The Autumn Semester normally begins in July/August and the Spring Semester normally begins in January.

Each regular semester has fourteen weeks for instruction. The final two weeks are designated for the End-Semester Examination, and one week during the semester is designated for the Mid-Semester Examination.

The summer vacation may include Summer School and supplementary examinations.

The Institute's Academic Calendar specifies dates for activities such as:
- Orientation
- Registration and Late Registration
- Commencement of Classes
- Adding and Dropping Courses
- Document submission
- Examinations
- Submission of Grades
- Vacation
- Mid-Semester Recess
- Official student activities

The Academic Calendar is approved by the Senate and is notified for each semester or academic year by the Dean/Associate Dean (Academic).
items.title: Academic Calendar
items.heading: Academic Calendar

items.text:

The DUPC oversees undergraduate academic matters within a department.

- Head of the Department: Chairperson.
- Faculty Advisor for each batch, nominated by the concerned Head of Department.
- Two undergraduate student members with CGPA of at least 8.50, elected by undergraduate students of the third and/or fourth years.

Undergraduate Academic Committees — Institute Undergraduate Program Committee (IUPC)
The IUPC oversees undergraduate academic matters at the institute level.

items.heading: Institute Undergraduate Program Committee (IUPC)

items.text:
Undergraduate Academic Committees — Composition
- Dean/Associate Dean, Academic Affairs: Chairperson.

items.text:
B.Tech Programme Overview — B.Tech Programme Overview
The B.Tech programme at IIIT Bhagalpur is governed by the rules and regulations in the B.Tech Ordinances. The ordinance applies to existing disciplines and to new disciplines introduced under the B.Tech programme.

A student becomes eligible for the B.Tech degree after fulfilling the prescribed academic requirements and required extra-academic activities.

The ordinance describes the four-year B.Tech programme and currently lists these branches:
- Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
- Electronics & Communication Engineering (ECE)
- Mechatronics and Automation Engineering (MAE)
- Mathematics and Computing (MNC)

The provisions may also apply to new disciplines introduced in the future.

Once approved by the Governing Body/Board of Governors, this ordinance supersedes corresponding earlier academic rules and regulations and is binding on students.

The Senate retains the authority to modify or relax regulations from time to time. Changes affecting students admitted in earlier years are to be handled so that those students are not placed in an unfair situation.
items.title: B.Tech Programme Overview
items.heading: B.Tech Programme Overview

items.text:
Late Registration — Late Registration
A student who does not register on the day or days announced in the Academic Calendar may be permitted to complete late registration when there is a compelling reason.

Late registration:
- must occur within the period notified by the Institute;
- requires payment of the prescribed late fee;
- normally cannot be permitted after one week, or after the deadline specified in the Academic Calendar.

The applicable deadline is therefore the one notified in the Institute's Academic Calendar.
items.title: Late Registration
items.heading: Late Registration

items.text:
B.Tech Course Registration — B.Tech Course Registration
Every student must register for approved courses through the assigned Faculty Advisor at the beginning of each semester on the date specified in the Academic Calendar.

The Dean/Associate Dean of Academic Affairs may cancel registration for one or more courses if the registration violates applicable rules.

Students are required to be physically present in their respective departments during registration.

A student is permitted to register only when:
- previous-semester fees and fines, if any, have been cleared;
- required fees for the current semester have been paid; and
- the student has not been debarred from registration on a specific ground.

A student must pass all first-year courses before registering for third-year (5th semester) courses.

Students admitted to the first year must submit all documents prescribed by the Institute at registration.

A student who misses the scheduled registration may be allowed late registration within the notified period for a compelling reason and on payment of the prescribed late fee. Normally, late registration is not permitted after one week or after the period specified in the Academic Calendar.
items.title: B.Tech Course Registration
items.heading: B.Tech Course Registration

items.text:
Residence and Hostel Requirements — 10.1 Hostel Accommodation
Students who are assigned hostel accommodation by the Institute authorities must:

- Reside in the allotted room.
- Avail the Mess facility.
- Pay Hostel Rent.
- Pay other applicable hostel-related fees.
items.title: Residence and Hostel Requirements
items.heading: 10.1 Hostel Accommodation

items.text:
Residence and Hostel Requirements — 10.2 Relaxation of Fees
Under special circumstances, the Director may relax:

- Hostel rent
- Hostel-related fees
- Mess Fee
items.title: Residence and Hostel Requirements
items.heading: 10.2 Relaxation of Fees

items.text:
Residence and Hostel Requirements — 10.3 Married Accommodation
No married accommodation shall be provided to any student of the undergraduate courses.
items.title: Residence and Hostel Requirements
items.heading: 10.3 Married Accommodation

items.text:
Residence and Hostel Requirements — 10.4 Hostel Rules
All students must abide by the rules and regulations of the hostel as framed from time to time by the Hostel Affairs' Board.
items.title: Residence and Hostel Requirements
items.heading: 10.4 Hostel Rules
